questions.question: Although animal and plant cells are often drawn flat on a page, what is their actual shape in real life?
options: They are completely flat and two-dimensional
They have a three-dimensional shape
They are perfect hollow cylinders
They change into random shapes every second

questions.question: Which of the following lists contains only structures commonly found in animal cells?
options: Chloroplast, cell wall, nucleus
Cytoplasm, cell membrane, nucleus, mitochondria
Vacuole, cell wall, cytoplasm
Mitochondria, chloroplast, vacuole, cell membrane

questions.question: What is the main function of the mitochondria in an animal cell?
options: To control all the activities of the cell
To release energy through respiration
To store genetic material
To hold the cell together and act as a barrier

questions.question: What is a unicellular organism?
options: An organism made of a single living cell
An organism made of exactly two cells
An organism with no cells at all
An organism with millions of cells

questions.question: Which statement is true about multicellular organisms?
options: They are made of only one cell that does every job
They are made of multiple cells, and all cells do the exact same job
They are made of more than one cell, and different cells perform different jobs
They do not contain any specialized cells

questions.question: In multicellular organisms, what is formed when similar cells join together to perform a specific job?
options: An organ system
A tissue
A unicellular organism
An organelle

questions.question: What is the correct scientific term for a group of different tissues working together to perform a specific job?
options: An organ
An organ system
An organism
A cell colony

questions.question: What are the living building blocks that make up all organisms?
options: Atoms
Cells
Tissues
Organs

questions.question: Why do we need a microscope to see individual cells?
options: Because cells are usually too small to see with the unaided eye
Because cells only exist inside dark rooms
Because cells are transparent and have no mass
Because cells move too fast to be seen by humans

questions.question: Which scientific instrument is most commonly used in a school laboratory to observe cells on a prepared slide?
options: A magnifying glass
A telescope
A light microscope
A spectroscope

questions.question: Which of these is a true statement about plant cells?
options: Plant cells do not have a nucleus
Plant cells have some common structures shared across different plants
Plant cells are exactly identical to animal cells in every way
Plant cells lack a cytoplasm

questions.question: Which of the following structures is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
options: Nucleus
Mitochondria
Cell wall
Cytoplasm

questions.question: What is the function of the permanent vacuole in a plant cell?
options: To carry out photosynthesis
To control what enters and leaves the cell
To contain cell sap and help keep the cell firm
To release energy from glucose

questions.question: What is the main reason for adding a chemical stain to a cell sample before viewing it under a microscope?
options: To kill any bacteria on the slide
To make it easier to see some parts of the cells
To glue the cover slip down tightly
To change the magnification of the lens

questions.question: How should observations from a light microscope be recorded in a science notebook?
options: As a colorful oil painting
As a scientific line drawing
As a detailed written paragraph only
As a 3D clay model

questions.question: What makes specialised cells different from general cells?
options: They have shapes, sizes, and structures adapted for the specific jobs they do
They can live outside an organism indefinitely
They contain no genetic material
They do not require nutrients to survive

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a specialised plant cell?
options: Red blood cell
Nerve cell
Root hair cell
Muscle cell

questions.question: Which of the following statements about life processes is correct?
options: Only animals undergo life processes
Plants do not require any life processes
The same basic life processes happen in all living organisms
Unicellular organisms do not carry out life processes

questions.question: Which of these is a complete list of life processes shared by all living organisms?
options: Movement, reproduction, sensitivity, growth, respiration, excretion, nutrition
Breathing, walking, thinking, sleeping, eating, growing, talking
Photosynthesis, digestion, circulation, hearing, running, smelling
Melting, freezing, evaporating, condensing, dissolving, burning

questions.question: Under what condition is movement considered a true sign of life for an organism?
options: When the organism is carried by the wind
When the organism moves itself to achieve something
When the organism is washed away by water
When the organism expands due to heat
